mcqs.learning_point: Understand the meaning of parallel lines
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes parallel lines?

options.A: Parallel lines intersect at one point.
options.B: Parallel lines are always the same distance apart and never meet.

mcqs.answer: Parallel lines are always the same distance apart and never meet.
mcqs.explanation: Parallel lines lie in the same plane, are equidistant at every point, and never intersect. Option B states this correctly. Option A is false because parallel lines do not intersect. Option C describes perpendicular lines, not parallel. Option D is incorrect because parallel lines are straight, not curved.

mcqs.question: In a diagram, line AB is drawn horizontally, line CD is also drawn horizontally, and line EF is drawn slanting downwards. Which pair of lines are parallel?
mcqs.explanation: Lines AB and CD are both horizontal, meaning they have the same direction and will never meet, so they are parallel. The slanted line EF is not parallel to either horizontal line, making options B and C incorrect. Option D is false because a parallel pair does exist (AB and CD).

mcqs.question: Figure I shows two lines that run in the same direction without meeting. Figure II shows two lines that cross each other. Which figure(s) contain parallel lines?
mcqs.explanation: In Figure I the lines are oriented the same way and never intersect, which is the definition of parallel lines. In Figure II the lines intersect, so they are not parallel. Therefore only Figure I contains parallel lines. Options B, C, and D are incorrect based on this reasoning.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise parallel lines in everyday surroundings
mcqs.question: Which of the following everyday situations contains a pair of parallel lines?

options.A: The edges of a closed book when opened
options.B: The two sides of a road that diverge
options.C: The opposite edges of a rectangular table
options.D: The arms of a clock at 3 o'clock

mcqs.answer: The opposite edges of a rectangular table
mcqs.explanation: The opposite edges of a rectangular table are straight and run in the same direction, never meeting, thus they are parallel. In option A the pages of an opened book meet at the spine, not parallel. In option B the road sides diverge, so they are not parallel. In option D the clock arms meet at the center, so they are not parallel. Hence option C is correct.
